messages:
Sam: quick heads-up — noticed regression after last night's kernel-selection change. short-seq SLOs (<=64 tokens) show +8-12ms host-side overhead at p50. canaries: 3/10 hosts. flame link: https://internal/fg/9054321000.svg :eyes:
Maya: saw the same on the canary dashboard, p95 also crept up ~15ms for some routes. good catch. which commit?
Sam: commit 2b7f4a5 toggled prefer-lzw=true in kernel-selector. hypothesis: extra memcpy/marshalling for small sequences. attaching small perf run results below.
Ben: quick skim of pprof showed heavy time in ingress::proto::unpack -> parse_frame and syscall writev spikes. also `sched_yield` appears more often.
Oliver: confirm — new kernel path adds an intermediate tensor packing step to align to 64B for vector kernels. helps large seqs but costs small ones. we missed the fallback fastpath.
Priya: KV cache metrics: miss rate +3% for the same window, which increases backend requests and host parsing. possible that route id hashing changed with the new packing metadata.
Sam: paste of the hot stacks I captured: ```
# perf top sample
  ingress::proto::unpack
  host::tokenize::process
  grpc::Writev
  kernel_selector::choose
```
Maya: interesting — grpc writev batching looks worse. Are we writing more small iovecs now?
Ben: yes — iovecs per request increased from ~2 to ~5 on the canaries. increased syscall count per RPC. quick mitigation: coalesce iovecs at host-side layer before calling writev. 1ms batching window saved ~6ms in local tests.
Oliver: another mitigation: revert `--prefer-lzw` flag for the short-seq canary pool while we fix selector heuristics. deploy-bot, can we rollback that flag for canary?
deploy-bot: rollback of feature flag `prefer-lzw` on canary pool initiated (id: ff-905432) at 2026-03-20T22:06:45Z. 2 hosts impacted. :white_check_mark:
Maya: thanks. we should also add a fastpath in `proto::unpack`: if payload_len < 256 and seq_len < 64, skip deep packing and use simple slice view. trivial change, low risk.
Sam: agree. I'll draft PR for preparse fastpath and iovec coalescing. Oliver — can you run microbench (`wrk` script) comparing before/after? Ben — can you run system-wide flamegraphs for a 60s window and share?
Oliver: running wrk now against canary fixture. will post numbers in ~30m.
Ben: scheduling perf run: `perf record -F 99 -p $(pidof host-preproc) -g -- sleep 60` then `perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl | flamegraph.pl > canary-out.svg`. will upload results to the thread when done.
Priya: I'll audit routing keys to confirm no change in hash input after selector change. if keys shifted, that explains KV miss bump.
Maya: follow-up items: 1) revert flag on canary (done), 2) PR for fastpath + iovec coalesce, 3) KV hash audit, 4) perf runs and flamegraphs, 5) add regression alert on p50 short-seq host-overhead.
Sam: assigning owners: PR (Sam), bench (Oliver), flame (Ben), kv-audit (Priya), alert (Maya). I'll update the regression board: https://internal/boards/regressions/905432
Priya: noted. will also check if any model variant fallbacks cause different tokenization format.
Maya: thanks team. quick reminder — keep logs (raw traces) for 2 weeks so SRE can correlate if the rollback doesn't fully recover. :thumbsup:
Sam: will do. ping me with any new data.
